> 
> ```
> 02-05 14:44:38.876 27243 27445 E godot   : ERROR: Condition "!_start_success" is true. Returning: 1
> 02-05 14:44:38.876 27243 27445 E godot   :    at: start (main/main.cpp:3888)
> ```

That error only pops up after other ones have failed previously, is there anything else towards the start of the log?

> On Samsung Galaxy XR, it also fails to start, but instead I get a popup that says:

> Please try exporting your game using the 'gl_compatibility' renderer.

> These are the log messages just before the `!_start_success` starts looping:
> 
> ```
> 02-06 12:53:39.509 13453 13523 I godot   : OpenXR: Failed to create Vulkan device [ XR_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILURE ]
> ```

This message is probably the key here. Is there any particular initialization requirements for this OpenXR function to suceed? Perhaps using a custom instance creation function instead? My PR moved around the Vulkan context initialization to be able to be done globally, and that doesn't seem to have failed at all.

Are you able to track whether `DisplayServerAndroid::check_vulkan_global_context` has been called before it gets to the OpenXR initialization? Is it possible there's some hooks it should've called instead by that point that are specific to OpenXR?

When using OpenXR, Godot isn't supposed to initialize Vulkan directly itself, it's supposed to do it through the OpenXR runtime. That's usually facilitated in Godot through `VulkanHooks`.

So, if https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114922 means we're completely bypassing that, then that could be the problem. Or, if it means we're now initializing Vulkan through OpenXR correctly, but we're doing it twice without fully cleaning up the first time through OpenXR, that could also be the issue

I'll spend some time trying to understand the implications of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114922

> I'll spend some time trying to understand the implications of [#114922](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114922)

That PR effectively moves the initialization of the Vulkan context to be done through a global variable located in the Android Display server, so it could be that it's now creating the context before the hooks themselves are installed for that to work. Figuring out the order here through printing or debugger stepping will likely make that obvious.

A brief look tells me OpenXRAPI::initialize is responsible for creating the extension, which in itself is the VulkanHooks, and is called from somewhere. The problem now is probably that it's called _after_ the Java method I pointed out before is called. Would it be too difficult to move the initialization of it to be done before that is called?

> so it could be that it's now creating the context before the hooks themselves are installed for that to work

I added a bunch of print statements, and, you're right, this appears to be exactly what's happening.

We've got:

- `RenderingContextDriverVulkan::initialize()` leads to `_initialize_devices()`
- `_initialize_devices()` will call into `VulkanHooks` if it's set, but it's not set at this point
- Later on, OpenXR is initialized and `VulkanHooks` is set, but it missed the chance to get the Vulkan physical device through OpenXR

> Would it be too difficult to move the initialization of it to be done before that is called?

It's tricky.

Currently, `OpenXRAPI::initialize()` is called in `initialize_openxr_module()` on `MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SERVERS`, which is an OK place for a module to do some initialization. I tried moving it to even `MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_CORE`, and that's still not early enough.

I'm not sure of a clean way to move a bit of module initialization earlier than that bit of platform initialization, but I'll keep poking around at it...

There's also a bit of a circular problem, in that `OpenXRAPI::initialize()` needs to be called with the name of the rendering driver that we're going to use, but the code we're trying to run before, is the code that decides which rendering driver we're going to use.

> There's also a bit of a circular problem, in that `OpenXRAPI::initialize()` needs to be called with the name of the rendering driver that we're going to use, but the code we're trying to run before, is the code that decides which rendering driver we're going to use.

This is indeed a major part of it all. OpenXR has become responsible for setting up the GPU when using Vulkan (design flaw of the century, but it was the only way they could do certain things), So we must know that we're about to use Vulkan, but we shouldn't have Vulkan already initialised.

I guess that's a huge catch-22 when we need to setup Vulkan, in order to find out that Vulkan isn't capable enough and fallback to OpenGL.

Frankly I'm surprised we haven't run into issues yet on any of the other platforms, or has this been merged so recently that I just haven't gotten around to running into serious problems yet?

> Frankly I'm surprised we haven't run into issues yet on any of the other platforms, or has this been merged so recently that I just haven't gotten around to running into serious problems yet?

The change in initialization order was only on Android, and it was merged only ~2 weeks ago (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114922)

> Frankly I'm surprised we haven't run into issues yet on any of the other platforms, or has this been merged so recently that I just haven't gotten around to running into serious problems yet?

The major change has been that Vulkan initialization was moved earlier because Android itself was possibly creating the wrong surface type as it had an assumption of what rendering device driver was in use even if Godot itself fell back to another option, as it basically had to do its best to replicate the logic of the C++ side on the Java side. The PR that David pointed to mostly addresses that. Otherwise it could create a Vulkan surface but fail upon trying to create the OpenGL driver instead.

I think the big flaw here is that there's no mechanism for providing the whole "VulkanHooks" class explicitly to the context driver / display server, and the decision to rely on it as a global has come back as an issue after refactoring this as it relies on the not-too-obvious initialization order.

If the code is refactored to be able to provide this explicitly to it in some way I think it'll be more evident how it can possibly be fixed and make it resilient against breaking in the future. I realize the tricky part here is that because it's a module, it might be a bit harder to hook up, but I believe it should be possible.

> I think the big flaw here is that there's no mechanism for providing the whole "VulkanHooks" class explicitly to the context driver / display server, and the decision to rely on it as a global has come back as an issue after refactoring this as it relies on the not-too-obvious initialization order.

Getting `VulkanHooks` to available to the context driver / display server earlier is only part of the problem.

What `VulkanHooks` needs to do in the context of OpenXR will only actually work if we've already initialized OpenXR.

(And this is complicated even further by the fact that initializing OpenXR depends on requesting all the OpenXR extensions we want, and that list is affected by GDExtensions, which are also tied to module initialization levels.)

So, to solve this, I really think we need to also bring part of the Android platform's initialization later, so that OpenXR can be initialized before it attempts to start creating Vulkan resources.
